paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The woman looks AMAZING. Purple, scarlet, gold, pearls, a golden cup. But John sees that the cup is full of "abominations," and he says she is "drunk with the blood of the saints and witnesses for Jesus" (Revelation 17:4, 6). Shiny on the outside doesn't make it good on the inside, and that's the first thing this passage teaches.

Second, look at who's really in charge. The beast, the ten kings and the woman all look powerful. But the angel says the kings get only "one hour of authority," and that God "has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose" until "the words of God are fulfilled" (Revelation 17:12, 17). Nobody in this passage is running loose. I think that's good news for any baker who has watched the loud, big-looking things of this world and wondered who's holding the timer.

Third, the Lamb wins. The kings "will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings" (Revelation 17:14). And He brings His "called and chosen and faithful ones" with Him. Friend, that's why my ovens stay ready. This story isn't over, and the ending is already settled.
